subject: Request: temporary overnight SLA carveout for scheduled migration
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam@uptownhealth.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@uptownhealth.com
Date: 2027-10-05T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: temporary overnight SLA carveout for scheduled migration

Hi Priyom,

We have a planned data migration and network maintenance scheduled for Oct 20-24 (Uptown Health, PT). During the nightly window (00:00–06:00 PT) we expect an increased incidence of P1 incidents related to transient service degradations — mostly read/write contention during DB switchover. Our internal ops team is proposing we accept a slightly relaxed external-RTO for those nights to avoid unnecessary escalations that would introduce more risk.

Specifically, can Redwood temporarily relax the P1 response SLA from 1 hour to 4 hours overnight (00:00–06:00 PT) for that date range, with the following caveats:
- We will operate in a maintenance posture (reduced writes) and accept read-only fallback where applicable.
- We need continuity for audit logs and call traces for postmortem.
- Procurement may require an amendment/DocuSign for the change.

I attached our maintenance plan for context (uptown-maintenance-plan.pdf). Would appreciate a short confirmation and any questions.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Head of Platform Ops, Uptown Health
Attachment: uptown-maintenance-plan.pdf

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@uptownhealth.com>
Cc: Uptown Health Ops <uptown-health-ops@uptownhealth.com>
Date: 2027-10-05T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary overnight SLA carveout for scheduled migration

Hi Liam — thanks for the heads-up and for the plan. A few clarifying q's before I loop in the on-call and engineering:
1) Confirming all times in PT (UTC-7) — correct?
2) Do you expect a consistent elevated incident rate across all nights or a spike concentrated on the first two nights?
3) Is read-only fallback explicitly acceptable to your product teams for all downstream user journeys, or only a subset?

Operationally we can propose a containment approach rather than a full 4-hour carveout:
- Containment window 00:00–06:00 PT where Redwood routes higher-risk requests to a read-only variant or cold fallback model variant, and we enable an automated retry/backoff on the client side.
- Standby on-call escalation: we can provide a single on-call engineer with a 2-hour P1 response guarantee, and a secondary 'on-call+escalation' contact on pager if containment fails.

If that model works we will need:
- A runbook addendum (we can prepare a draft).
- DocuSign amendment for the temporary SLA adjustment.
- Agreement on audit log retention for the window.

I've attached a quick support-bridge spreadsheet to capture on-call shifts and contacts (support-bridge-rotation.xlsx). Can you confirm timezone and which nights are most critical?

— Priyom
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachment: support-bridge-rotation.xlsx

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-05T11:26:00-07:00
Subject: FWD: Request: temporary overnight SLA carveout for scheduled migration

Team — forwarding request from Uptown Health (see below). High level: they want a temporary overnight SLA exception for Oct 20-24 during a DB migration. They proposed 4-hr P1 overnight; I suggested containment + 2-hr guaranteed P1 with standby.

Questions for approvals/ops:
- Can engineering accept a temporary 2-hr P1 for the window with automated fallback routing?
- Will this require an on-call shift change (we will need a named roster)?
- Any compliance objections on audit logs and retention?

CC'd Lauren for manager approval and procurement considerations.

On Oct 5, 2027, at 9:12 AM, Liam O'Connor <liam@uptownhealth.com> wrote:
> Hi Priyom,
> 
> We have a planned data migration and network maintenance scheduled for Oct 20-24 (Uptown Health, PT). During the nightly window (00:00–06:00 PT) we expect an increased incidence of P1 incidents related to transient service degradations — mostly read/write contention during DB switchover. Our internal ops team is proposing we accept a slightly relaxed external-RTO for those nights to avoid unnecessary escalations that would introduce more risk.
> 
> Specifically, can Redwood temporarily relax the P1 response SLA from 1 hour to 4 hours overnight (00:00–06:00 PT) for that date range, with the following caveats:...

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-05T13:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FWD: Request: temporary overnight SLA carveout for scheduled migration

Thanks for the ping — quick technical take:
- I can sign off on temporary relaxation but I'd prefer a narrower guaranteed RTO: 2 hours for P1 during the 00:00–06:00 PT window, with the containment routing enabled. That preserves a stronger SLA while acknowledging higher noise.
- We should implement an automated fallback path (model variant + read-only routing) to avoid manual intervention for the majority of cases.
- Engineering will designate one primary and one secondary on-call for those nights; I'll update our rota and provide names within 24 hours.
- We will update the runbook and add a short checklist for post-window verification (log pull, trace correlation).

Operational note: this will increase cross-region egress and minor compute costs because of replication/fallback behavior. Recommend we capture cost delta in an amendment but not block the exception.

Karthik
Director, Serving Runtime

From: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-06T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: FWD: Request: temporary overnight SLA carveout for scheduled migration

Agree with Karthik's narrower approach. Approve the temporary exception under these conditions:
- Temporary P1 RTO of 2 hours for Oct 20–24, 00:00–06:00 PT only.
- On-call roster with named primary and secondary (must be shared with Uptown before Oct 14).
- Updated runbook and post-window verification checklist added to the support ticket.
- DocuSign amendment signed by Uptown (Procurement) that includes cost delta language and the exact time window.
- Audit log retention extended by 90 days for events generated during the window.

Monica/Stephanie: please coordinate on-call scheduling and ensure we have one escalation path directly to me if the containment fails.

Lauren Bishop
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam@uptownhealth.com>, Uptown Health Ops <uptown-health-ops@uptownhealth.com>, procurement@uptownhealth.com
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica@redwood.com>, Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-10-06T17:45:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: temporary overnight SLA carveout for scheduled migration — Redwood confirmation and next steps

Liam — thanks for the patience. Redwood can accommodate a temporary SLA amendment for Uptown Health with the following binding conditions:

1) Effective window: 2027-10-20 00:00 PT through 2027-10-24 06:00 PT.
2) Temporary P1 RTO during the window: 2 hours (instead of 1 hour). P2 unchanged.
3) Containment/fallback: Redwood will enable read-only fallback routing and an automated model variant routing for the window; most incidents will be contained automatically.
4) On-call: primary and secondary named engineers will be provided by Oct 14 and listed in the runbook.
5) Audit/logging: Uptown must accept an extension of 90 days for event retention for records generated during the window.
6) Amendment: Procurement must sign the DocuSign amendment for the temporary change (DocuSign link: https://www.docusign.com/sign/uptown-ds-2027-10-06).
7) Cost & billing: fallback routing may incur minor cross-region egress and compute costs; we'll record the delta on the HubSpot deal (HUBSPOT-98765) and include cost language in the amendment.

Attachments enclosed: redwood-runbook-draft.pdf (draft runbook addendum) and support-bridge-rotation.xlsx (on-call roster template).

Next steps:
- Priyom to share the runbook draft and the named on-call contacts by Oct 14.
- Uptown to return a signed DocuSign amendment before Oct 18.
- Post-window verification call to be scheduled for Oct 25.

If this aligns please reply-all to confirm and I'll open the formal support ticket and the HubSpot amendment.

Thanks,
Priyom Das
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-runbook-draft.pdf; support-bridge-rotation.xlsx
